title: operator_desk.py: decisions, rulings, operator verdicts, wave gates, commit and push
acceptance_criteria: Build .harness/bin/operator_desk.py with decisions, rule, verdict, gate, commit and push as design section 5 specifies. Rulings are new append-only R files; dated records are never edited.

verdict acts as agent operator through blackboard.py, only on a task in review, and refuses when the operator produced it. commit and push follow safety rule 6: leak scan first, refuse on a hit, diff stat shown, current branch only, never main, never force.
gate writes the decision into the run's run.json under the shape of design section 3, through a function flow_runner.py can also call (agree the function name in your handoff).

.harness/tests/test_operator_desk.py per design section 8, in throwaway git repos; no test pushes anywhere real. Edit only operator_desk.py and its test, and create .harness/decisions/ and .harness/rulings/ with a README each. Run only your own test file. Hand off to verifier.

notes.note:
HANDOFF -> verifier: operator_desk.py built: decisions, rule, verdict, gate, commit, push; README for decisions/ and rulings/. test_operator_desk.py: 69 passed (fast_tests.py, own file only). 9 mutants (main allowed, force flag, push/commit skip scan, self-verdict, gate any status, added-lines-only broken, ruling overwrite, any choice) all killed.
Interfaces for other parts: record_gate_decision(root, run_id, decision, note="", by="operator", via="cli") -> run dict, decision is "approve" or "reject", raises operator_desk.Refused; sets run.status and gate.status to approved/rejected plus gate.decided/by/note/via, keeps gate.suite; locks <run dir>/.run.lock (flow_runner should take the same lock for its own run.json writes). Console-facing: decisions(root, status) -> (cards, problems); rule(root, id, choice, note, via="console"); verdict(root, T-id, "done"|"open", note); commit(root, message_file, dry_run, extra, stat_out); push(root, remote, dry_run, extra, stat_out). All raise Refused with a plain message (CLI exit 2). root is the repo root.
Env HARNESS_LEAK_TERMS (comma list) adds operator terms to the scan; sibling-project names are never in the repo.

VERIFIED by verifier-ui-desk. Replayed test_operator_desk.py: 69 passed. Read operator_desk.py against design sections 2, 3, 5: rule uses link(2) for new R files, verdict refuses non-review tasks and operator-produced tasks and a bare root, gate is one locked function, commit scans the exact bytes it commits, push sends only refs/heads/<current>:refs/heads/<current>, never main or master, no force or plus or tags. 14 mutants in a throwaway copy, all caught: rule overwrite (replace, fixed id, second ruling), push main allowed, push skips scan, commit skips scan, commit message not scanned, verdict any status, verdict self ok, plus refspec, force flag, --tags, push range widened, gate any status, added-lines filter broken. Shipped files scan clean. Residual (not blocking): sibling-project names need HARNESS_LEAK_TERMS; push does not fetch, so a stale tracking ref only widens the scan; git add -A commits the whole pending set; a case-insensitive remote could treat 'Main' as main (edge).
